clue.text: Termination of contract after a shoe fetish is revealed

indicators.note: the final letter is placed after the earlier pieces in the clue's reading

parts.note: a mule is a backless slipper or shoe

indicators.note: a termination is an end, so the final letter of the word contract is taken

explanation.surface: A contract ends once someone's shoe obsession comes to light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fetish' looks like part of the shoe story, but it is the definition: a charm believed to have magical power.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish in its older sense is an object worn or kept for supposed protective magic, like a charm.

clue.text: Note the least bit of hesitation is absent

indicators.note: being absent means these letters are missing from the longer word

parts.note: the least possible amount is the minimum
um is the little noise of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A remark that this note shows not even the slightest hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove UM from the end of MINIMUM ('is absent').
explanation.definitionFit: In music a minim is a half note, worth two crotchets.

clue.text: Pub diet?

definitions.meaning: one's nearest pub, the regular haunt
a slimming diet is low in calories; the question mark flags the pun

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as LO-CAL, short for low-calorie, and a dieter's food fits.
explanation.definitionFit: British drinkers call their nearest regular pub their local; low-calorie food is labelled with the same letters.

clue.text: Relation of Swiss folk hero in German capital

parts.note: William Tell is the legendary Swiss archer and folk hero

indicators.note: a capital letter heads a word, so capital here means the first letter of German, not a city

explanation.surface: Someone related to William Tell living in Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' is not Berlin but the first letter of German. 'Relation' means a narration, not a relative.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation of events is a recounting of them, as when a story is narrated.

clue.text: Unrestricted items for discussion are entertaining, at last: from Constable to Monet

indicators.note: with no restrictions, the word loses its limits, its first and last letters

parts.note: an agenda is the list of items to discuss at a meeting

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so one piece sits inside the other
at last points to the final letter of the word that follows it

explanation.surface: A trip through art history from the English painter Constable to the French painter Monet.
explanation.walkthrough: AGENDA trimmed gives GEND; ARE holds M, the last letter of 'from'. The painters' names suggest art, but a constable to Frenchman Monet is a French policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: A French police officer, the equivalent of a British constable, is a gendarme, so a Frenchman would use that word.

clue.text: Try to cast youngster with webbed feet

parts.note: to have a go is to try
to sling something is to throw or cast it

explanation.surface: An attempt to cast a young duck-footed child in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests the theatre, but here it means throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is a gosling, and geese have webbed feet.

clue.text: Possibly 3 million neural folds

indicators.note: something that folds collapses out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A neuroscience note about the brain's three million neural folds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folds' rearranges M and NEURAL together. '3' is an example of the definition, hence 'Possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The figure 3 is a number written as a symbol, a written digit.

clue.text: American books on a Roman Catholic jerk from the far South?

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible
a tic is an involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: A twitchy American reading books about a Catholic from far down south.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as loose: the answer describes what comes from the region round the South Pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar region round the South Pole is the furthest south one can go.

clue.text: Men's faith is wavering in underground passage

indicators.note: faith that is wavering is unsteady and moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Miners losing their faith deep down a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical tunnel dug down into a mine is an underground passage for miners and ore.

clue.text: Unfortunate scratching walls after overturning centre of drinking joints

indicators.note: the trimmed word comes after the reversed letters
overturning turns the picked letters back to front
the centre of the word drinking is its two middle letters
scratching out the walls removes the outer letters

parts.note: someone unfortunate is luckless

explanation.surface: An unlucky drinker in some seedy bars, scraping the walls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of drinking' gives NK, which 'overturning' makes KN; LUCKLESS loses its walls to give UCKLES. 'drinking joints' looks like bars; 'joints' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The finger joints are the bony knobs we rap on a door with.

clue.text: Largely quiet, very little rebellion

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to keep mum is to stay quiet
tiny means very small

explanation.surface: A rebellion that was mostly silent and very small.
explanation.walkthrough: MUM loses its last letter ('Largely') to give MU.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt by sailors or soldiers against their officers is the classic shipboard rebellion.

clue.text: Ingredient in chocolate lures me, if I stray

indicators.note: to stray is to wander off, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A dieter tempted by chocolate: it lures me if I wander from the plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Lecithin is added to chocolate to keep fat and solids blended; such an additive is this kind of binding agent.

clue.text: Possibility that doctor is kissing nurses

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the words hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A scandal: the chance that a doctor is kissing the nurses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurses' reads as hospital staff but means holds: the letters run across 'doctoR IS Kissing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk is a chance that something bad may happen.

clue.text: Fruit goes off; covering goes off

indicators.note: covering means the second group of letters wraps round the first
off again signals that these letters are rearranged

parts.note: goes as the plural of go, two attempts, gives go and go

indicators.note: fruit that goes off goes bad, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fruit spoils; then the wrapping round it spoils too.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'goes off' gives OSEG; the second reads 'goes' as two goes, GO GO, and 'off' shuffles them to GOOG, which is 'covering' OSEG.
explanation.definitionFit: The gooseberry is called this in informal British English, a dialect name for the fruit.

clue.text: Complete two umpiring decisions?

definitions.meaning: complete as in utter or thoroughgoing
a cricket umpire's verdict that a batter is dismissed, given twice and joined

explanation.walkthrough: A cricket umpire raises a finger to give a batter 'out'; twice, joined by 'and', builds the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something thorough and absolute, like an utter scoundrel, is complete in every respect.

clue.text: Little time to be impatient without initially seeming unforthcoming

parts.note: sec is short for second, a little time

indicators.note: without means the letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: restive means restless and impatient

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word seeming

explanation.surface: A moment's impatience, without seeming unhelpful at first.
explanation.walkthrough: RESTIVE loses S, the first letter of 'seeming' ('without initially'), leaving RETIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps things to themselves is guarded and reticent, not forthcoming.

clue.text: Allow Henry in terminal

parts.note: to let is to allow
Hal is a familiar short form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Let Henry into the airport terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terminal' suggests an airport, but it is an adjective: deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal illness is fatal, so terminal and deadly share a sense.

clue.text: Plaster mostly held firm

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: something held fast is stuck
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: Plaster that mostly held firm on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine plaster used to coat walls and mould decorations is a kind of render.

clue.text: Employment Act's subsection gets judge struck off, which is outrageous

indicators.note: struck off means removed, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a job is a piece of employment
a scene is a subdivision of an act in a play

explanation.surface: An outrage: a clause of the Employment Act lets a judge be struck off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' looks like legislation but is a division of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent or shocking behaviour is offensive enough to outrage people.

clue.text: Permitted to be inspired by whimsical joy

indicators.note: to be inspired, breathed in, by something is to sit inside it

parts.note: fey means whimsical or otherworldly
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: Something allowed being inspired by a whimsical sense of joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be inspired by' is taken literally: to be breathed in, so the permitted piece goes inside the whimsical one.
explanation.definitionFit: Felicity is great happiness, a formal word for joy or bliss.

clue.text: Plant releases iodine over area

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means above, so the earlier pieces sit on top of the last

parts.note: to free is to release
I is the chemical symbol for iodine

explanation.surface: A plant giving off iodine across a wide area.
explanation.definitionFit: Freesias are fragrant flowering plants grown from corms, popular as cut flowers.

clue.text: Shut up about British — essentially, they can't provide a service

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece surrounds the other
in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to seal is to shut

indicators.note: essentially means at its essence, the heart of the word

explanation.surface: Be quiet about the British: at heart they can't serve anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: SEAL turned 'up' gives LAES, which goes 'about' ITI, the core of 'British'. A service here is a church service, which lay people cannot conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay people, unlike ordained clergy, cannot officiate at religious worship.

clue.text: Spanish team, formerly

definitions.meaning: the Spanish word for eleven, the number in a football team
formerly means at one time in the past

explanation.surface: A former Spanish team.
explanation.walkthrough: A football side has eleven players, and once is Spanish for eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: Spanish for eleven names a side's player count; as an English adverb the word means at some earlier time.

clue.text: Expert in deformation of silicates doped with phosphorus

indicators.note: a semiconductor doped with an element has it added inside, so the letter goes in
deformation twists a shape out of true, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: P is the chemical symbol for phosphorus

explanation.surface: A materials scientist expert in deforming silicate crystals doped with phosphorus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deformation of' rearranges SILICATES, and 'doped with' inserts P.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist is someone with expert knowledge of one narrow field.

clue.text: Promise to scrub top shelf

indicators.note: to scrub the top is to remove the uppermost, first, letter in a down clue

parts.note: a pledge is a promise

explanation.surface: A promise to clean the top shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow flat projection from a wall or cliff serves as a shelf.

clue.text: Band took head of EMI to court

parts.note: took, completed by to court at the end of the clue, means sued: to sue someone is to take them to law

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A band sued its record label EMI.
explanation.walkthrough: Suede are a 1990s British indie rock band; EMI is a record company.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede were a leading Britpop group of the 1990s, so the name is that of a band.

clue.text: Person with diamonds in upper part of dress

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone wearing diamonds on the top half of their dress.
explanation.definitionFit: The fitted section of a dress above the waist is its bodice.

clue.text: Superficial type stops clock with tip of pen

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to clock something is slang for to see or notice it
a kind is a type or sort

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shallow sort of person stops a clock with the tip of a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is the slang verb meaning notice. KIND 'stops' SEE: it plugs the middle of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only on the surface, like beauty, goes no deeper than the outer layer of the body.

clue.text: Celtic centre occasionally starts to recruit artists and the like

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some letters, every other one
the starts of these words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Celtic's centre now and then starts recruiting artists and their like.
explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is a Scottish football club, so 'centre' suggests a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase meaning 'and other things' ends a list of similar items.

clue.text: Metal pin is more out of plane?

definitions.meaning: a metal spike for holding meat while it cooks
skew means out of line or not flat, so this is its comparative form

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as SKEW plus the comparative ending -ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A kebab or roasting spit is a long metal pin; the comparative of an adjective for askew means more crooked.
